disclosures: Wheeled rover (raycast-vehicle class): Rigid-body raycast vehicle, Coulomb friction, no soil mechanics. Verdicts valid for this model class only.
Quadruped (kinematic capability envelope): Kinematic capability envelope anchored to ANYmal published spec (footprint, max step, max slope). No gait simulation performed or implied.

Probe methodology: seeded probe rain with CCD; every fall-through cross-checked by an independent raycast at the probe's exit point before it counts as a hole. Surface confirmation counts a probe at rest OR sustained rolling contact (>= 0.5 s of continuous collider contact along its path — on slopes a ball never sleeps; its contact record is the experiment).
Trust states cover robot-REACHABLE space only; 'observed' means no physical experiment touched the cell.

Capture envelope: claims are limited to the splat capture envelope — collider columns whose visual coverage reaches this world's own surveyed-surface baseline. 12.2% of collider columns (~2 m²) lie beyond it and are OUTSIDE THE SURVEYED AREA: no defect, divergence, or fall-through evidence is drawn there. Absence of visual data beyond the capture is a capture limit, not an invisible wall.
393 of 816 probes exited the surveyed area (rolled off an open edge or beyond the capture envelope) — recorded as exits, excluded from all defect evidence.

Detection floor: at this coverage (ray grid 0.1 m, ~0.18 m probe spacing over the 28 m² surveyed area), 'verified' rules out collider holes with footprint ≥ ~0.20 m; smaller defects are below the instrument's floor.

Divergence threshold self-calibrated to this world's simplification noise floor: 0.500 m (1.5x the p99 splat-to-collider distance on probe-verified cells, height-banded to within 0.75 m of the contacted surface). 'Divergent' means splat/collider disagreement beyond the vendor's own demonstrated simplification tolerance.

Phantom-collider evidence radius self-calibrated to the shipped point cloud: 'no visual support' means no point within 0.20 m (1.5x the cloud's 0.02 m mean spacing over the surveyed area, bounded to [0.2, 0.6] m). The experiment defeats phantom evidence at the surface it validated: samples within 0.75 m of terrain a probe rested on or rolled across are excluded — geometry rising above a validated surface still counts.
Single-level survey: one walkable surface per column; multi-level worlds are unsupported in this version.
Scope of the grade: it predicts navmesh-level traversability under the disclosed model class. It does not predict policy transfer or visual-domain fidelity.
All measurements carry uncertainty ranges; the methods line under each number states how it was obtained.
